# Craft

- CRF-005: Classes follow SOLID: one reason to change (single responsibility), extended without being edited (open-closed), usable wherever their base type is (Liskov substitution), small interfaces shaped by their clients (interface segregation), and every dependency explicit, passed in as a constructor or method parameter, and pointing toward abstractions, never from business code to infrastructure details (dependency inversion, explicit dependencies).
- CRF-006: Keep concerns apart: business rules know nothing of UI, persistence or transport, and input is validated where it enters the system (a request, a message, a file, configuration), so the code inside can trust it; SEC-010 (proposed) says how an API validates a request.
- CRF-013: Follow Microsoft's dependency injection guidelines: a service never gets its dependencies from a service locator, a factory that resolves them at run time or static access to the container (CRF-005 says how they're passed in); a singleton never captures a scoped service, and no scoped service is resolved from the root; and the container validates scopes and its registrations (ValidateScopes, ValidateOnBuild) wherever the tests run the app.
- CRF-014: Types keep their state behind members that keep it valid (encapsulation), and the domain's ignorance of persistence (CRF-006) holds in what it references and in its shape: no persistence library, no persistence attributes and no constructor only the database needs.
